description: Voting Village presentations from DEF CON 27 covering voting systems security, election integrity, and vulnerabilities in digital voting infrastructure.

talks.title: Tod Beardsley - Securing Voting Systems Beyond Paper Ballots
talks.teaser: Securing voting systems beyond paper ballots—comprehensive approaches to election infrastructure protection.
talks.summary:
Tod Beardsley, Director of Research at Rapid7, examines the broader attack surface of U.S. election infrastructure in "Securing Voting Systems Beyond Paper Ballots," arguing that the national conversation on election security must look beyond optical scanners and paper ballots.

[05:46] Beardsley emphasizes that the decentralized architecture of American elections—comprising thousands of independent county and municipal jurisdictions operating under state-specific laws [11:13]—presents unique structural challenges. While paper ballots and voter-verifiable audit trails provide essential post-election verifiability, they do not protect against pre-election disruptions targeting voter registration databases, electronic pollbooks (e-pollbooks), or election night reporting portals.

[16:38] The talk outlines practical, actionable security measures that local election officials and county IT teams can implement ahead of election cycles without waiting for major federal overhauls. Beardsley highlights the importance of network segmentation, multi-factor authentication, routine vulnerability assessments, incident response planning, and establishing cooperative relationships with the cybersecurity research community to defend municipal IT networks from ransomware and targeted interference.

talks.title: Rahul Patel - Incident Lifecycle Incident Response Management Planning
talks.teaser: Incident lifecycle and response planning for election infrastructure emergencies.
talks.summary:
In this operational security presentation at the DEF CON 27 Voting Village, Rahul Patel and Tonya Rice from the Cook County Clerk's Office and Chicago Board of Election Commissioners discuss incident lifecycle management and rapid response planning for municipal elections. At 04:00, they describe the unique operational pressure of election day, where election administrators face an unforgiving, compressed timeframe with zero tolerance for prolonged system outages.

Rahul details proactive preparedness at 08:00, emphasizing that detection, containment, and restoration strategies must be fully tested and rehearsed well before voters arrive at polling stations. At 12:00, he introduces modular, single-page incident action runbooks designed to guide poll workers and technical triage teams through specific failure scenarios—such as electronic poll book sync errors or network link drops—without escalating into panic.

The speakers examine the operational differences between daytime polling hours and evening ballot tallying at 16:00, highlighting the shift in threat vectors once voting closes at 6:00 PM. They review collaborative governance at 20:00, showing how joint coordination between county and city election boards unifies incident logging. They conclude at 24:00 by detailing real-time communication protocols with federal agencies (DHS CISA) and private election software vendors throughout election night. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Marian Schneider - Voting Systems are Insecure Lets just Vote on Phones
talks.teaser: Marian Schneider Voting Systems are Insecure Lets just Vote on Phones - election security and voting system protection strategies.
talks.summary:
Marian Schneider, President of Verified Voting, presents a rigorous critique of internet and smartphone-based voting proposals in "Voting Systems are Insecure: Let's Just Vote on Phones." Schneider confronts the growing push to introduce mobile voting apps (such as Voatz and blockchain-backed voting platforms), deconstructing why mobile voting fundamentally undermines democratic integrity.

[04:04] Schneider begins by reviewing the documented cyber threats targeting election infrastructure, recalling nation-state reconnaissance against state voter registration databases and phishing campaigns against election software vendors. She outlines the foundational requirements of democratic elections [08:11]: guaranteeing voter eligibility and the "one person, one vote" principle while strictly preserving ballot secrecy and preventing coercion.

[12:20] The presentation details the insurmountable technical vulnerabilities of voting across mobile devices and internet portals. Schneider explains that consumer mobile devices are susceptible to client-side malware, operating system vulnerabilities, spyware, and credential theft, while internet transmission is vulnerable to denial-of-service (DoS) attacks and server-side manipulation. Crucially, because secret ballots cannot link a voter's identity to their vote, remote digital ballots lack voter-verifiable paper audit trails (VVPAT) [16:22], rendering post-election risk-limiting audits (RLAs) impossible. Schneider concludes that paper-based voting with manual auditability remains the only viable, resilient standard for national elections.

talks.title: Kevin Collier - What Role Can Journalists Play in Securing Elections
talks.teaser: Role of journalists in election security—reporting, awareness, and public oversight mechanisms.
talks.summary:
In this session at the DEF CON 27 Voting Village, veteran cybersecurity reporter Kevin Collier examines the role and responsibilities of journalism in covering election infrastructure security. He opens at 08:00 by discussing the fundamental challenge of communicating intricate technical security concepts clearly and responsibly to non-technical news consumers without sensationalizing risk or undermining voter faith in democratic institutions.

Kevin dissects media coverage trends at 16:00, analyzing the viral media frenzy surrounding youth participants hacking mock election results websites in the Voting Village, explaining how headlines conflated unofficial reporting displays with hardened tabulator machines. At 24:00, he explores investigative reporting into voting machine vendors, scrutinizing the use of cellular modems in optical scan tabulators and vulnerabilities in county election night reporting portals.

Reflecting on bipartisan security consensus at 32:00, Kevin discusses the widespread agreement among security researchers and election officials on the necessity of voter-verified paper ballots. At 40:00, he shares how journalists vet researcher credibility and verify technical claims before publishing. He closes at 48:00 with expectations for investigative press coverage leading up to the 2020 presidential election, focusing on regulatory accountability and supply chain security. talks.title: Joseph Marks - Panel
talks.teaser: Expert panel discussion on election security policy, governance, and multi-stakeholder coordination.
talks.summary:
Joseph Marks, cybersecurity reporter at Politico, moderates an extensive panel discussion at the DEF CON 27 Voting Village featuring election officials, security researchers, and policy experts examining the evolving state of election security leading up to the 2020 elections.

[17:49] The panelists review progress made since 2016 in coordinating threat intelligence sharing between the Department of Homeland Security (DHS/CISA), the Election Infrastructure ISAC (EI-ISAC), and state and local election administrators. They discuss the deployment of Albert network monitoring sensors, the distribution of federal Help America Vote Act (HAVA) grant funding, and the persistent resource disparities separating well-funded state election offices from under-resourced rural county clerks [33:23].

[49:01] The conversation turns to the complex relationship between voting machine manufacturers and the independent security research community. Panelists debate the legal protections, DMCA exemptions, and coordinated vulnerability disclosure policies necessary for researchers to ethically probe commercial voting machines without fear of legal reprisal. They conclude by discussing the nationwide push toward universal paper ballots, the technical implementation of risk-limiting audits (RLAs) [01:07:30], and strategies for combating disinformation intended to erode public confidence in election outcomes.

talks.title: Jason Hill - Asssessing Election Infrastructure
talks.teaser: Comprehensive assessment frameworks for evaluating election infrastructure security posture.
talks.summary:
In this informative briefing at the DEF CON 27 Voting Village, Jason Hill and Genevieve Marquart from the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA / DHS) detail the specialized election infrastructure assessment services offered by the National Cybersecurity Assessments and Technical Services (NCATS) team. At 04:00, they provide an overview of nine no-cost cybersecurity services available to state, county, and municipal election officials, ranging from external vulnerability scanning to in-depth Risk and Vulnerability Assessments (RVA).

The speakers discuss state-mandated security directives at 08:00, showing how jurisdictions are proactively leveraging federal technical support ahead of the 2020 general election. At 12:00, Jason explains the methodology behind external penetration testing on election networks, where operators test whether compromised low-privilege accounts can escalate privileges or pivot laterally into sensitive voter registration databases.

At 16:00, Genevieve explains the formal onboarding process for local election directors seeking DHS assistance. They highlight federal initiatives to migrate municipal election sites to secure .gov domains at 20:00, enhancing resilience against phishing and domain spoofing. They conclude at 24:00 by describing CISA's proactive threat hunting and incident response teams, which assist election administrators in rapid containment and digital forensics in the event of an active intrusion. talks.title: John Odum - Election Security Threats Posed by Very Small Jurisdictions
talks.teaser: John Odum Election Security Threats Posed by Very Small Jurisdictions - election security and voting system protection strategies.
talks.summary:
John Odum, City Clerk of Montpelier, Vermont, provides a boots-on-the-ground perspective on the unique cybersecurity threats facing small and rural election jurisdictions across the United States.

[04:51] Odum explains that while major metropolitan voting systems capture national media headlines, small towns and rural townships represent the soft underbelly of national election infrastructure. Local municipal clerks often manage voter registration databases using shared, multi-purpose municipal desktop computers that handle general city business, pay utility bills, and browse the web—all without dedicated IT staff, modern firewalls, or cybersecurity training [09:33].

[14:03] Because small-jurisdiction election systems possess administrative credentials that connect directly into centralized statewide voter registration databases, a compromise at the town clerk level can serve as a lateral jumping point into statewide voter registries. Odum discusses practical, low-cost mitigations, including regional shared IT security services, mandatory two-factor authentication, and the continued reliability of hand-counted paper ballots in small communities [20:22], urging state and federal agencies to direct cybersecurity resources directly to local municipal offices.

talks.title: Dr Philip Stark - Trustworthy Elections Evidence and Dispute Resolution
talks.teaser: Dr Philip Stark Trustworthy Elections Evidence and Dispute Resolution - election security and voting system protection strategies.
talks.summary:
In this keynote address at the DEF CON 27 Voting Village, Dr. Philip Stark, Professor of Statistics at UC Berkeley, outlines rigorous mathematical frameworks for verifiable democratic elections and evidence-based dispute resolution. He begins at 04:00 by challenging the premise of software trust in democratic elections, arguing that elections should never rely on blind faith in complex computer code, firmware, or vendor secrecy.

Dr. Stark presents the statistical mechanics of Risk-Limiting Audits (RLAs) at 08:00, explaining how this audit methodology provides strong mathematical guarantees of detecting and correcting incorrect contest outcomes by conducting systematic manual audits of paper ballots. At 12:00, he underscores the indispensable prerequisite for RLAs: an immutable, voter-verified physical paper trail, noting that any jurisdiction utilizing paper ballots can conduct rigorous risk-limiting audits.

Examining ongoing disputes within the election security community at 16:00, Dr. Stark analyzes the technical risks of universal Ballot Marking Devices (BMDs) versus hand-marked paper ballots, arguing that BMDs introduce software dependencies between voter intent and the physical record. He concludes at 24:00 by detailing how combining strongly software-independent voting systems, optical scanners, and robust hand-count audits establishes verifiable evidence necessary to resolve electoral challenges transparently. talks.title: Evanna Hu - While the Bots Distracted You Overt Russian Information Ops
talks.teaser: Evanna Hu While the Bots Distracted You Overt Russian Information Ops - election security and voting system protection strategies.
talks.summary:
Evanna Hu delivers a compelling analysis of Russian foreign influence operations in "While the Bots Distracted You: Overt Russian Information Ops," arguing that Western security discourse has focused excessively on automated social media bots while ignoring highly coordinated, overt state-sponsored media apparatuses.

[05:16] Hu traces the historical evolution of modern Russian information warfare doctrines, illustrating how principles articulated in military strategy (such as the Gerasimov doctrine [16:22]) view information warfare as a continuous, permanent operational domain rather than an activity confined to election seasons. She analyzes key geopolitical precursors, including the 2008 Russo-Georgian war [10:49], the 2014 Euromaidan protests, and the annexation of Crimea.

[22:09] The presentation examines the massive reach and narrative sophistication of state-controlled media outlets like RT (Russia Today) and Sputnik. Hu demonstrates how RT strategically amasses billions of views on YouTube and social media by broadcasting viral, culturally resonant, or controversial human-interest content before subtly weaving in state-aligned geopolitical narratives and societal grievances. She concludes by urging intelligence analysts and policy makers to look beyond automated bot-detection heuristics and focus on the strategic influence of state-backed overt information pipelines.

talks.title: Dr Linton Salmon - The DARPA SSITH Program at DEFCON
talks.teaser: Dr Linton Salmon The DARPA SSITH Program at DEFCON - election security and voting system protection strategies.
talks.summary:
In this presentation at the DEF CON 27 Voting Village, Dr. Linton Salmon, Program Manager at DARPA's Microsystems Technology Office, introduces the System Security Integration Through Hardware and Firmware (SSITH) program and invites the hacker community to evaluate its prototype hardware defenses. He opens at 05:00 by explaining the foundational philosophy of SSITH: rather than continuously patching software vulnerabilities, SSITH designs microarchitectures that eliminate entire classes of software exploits directly in silicon.

Dr. Salmon discusses why real-world offensive testing is critical at 10:00, stating that formal security proofs are insufficient without adversarial red-teaming by independent researchers. At 15:00, he demonstrates prototype FPGA systems implementing novel hardware protections against common vulnerability classes, including buffer overflows, return-oriented programming (ROP), code injection, and information leakage side channels.

He explains the crowdsourced testing engagement at 20:00, outlining the DEF CON bug bounty framework and inviting attendees to compromise the SSITH hardware prototypes. At 25:00, Dr. Salmon explores engineering tradeoffs between silicon area, clock speed, power consumption, and security guarantees. He concludes at 30:00 by addressing questions regarding how hardware-enforced memory safety distinguishes between malicious exploit primitives and benign developer bugs, highlighting applications for high-assurance electronic voting systems. talks.title: Alex Stanev - Machine Voting The Bulgarian Experience
talks.teaser: Alex Stanev Machine Voting The Bulgarian Experience - election security and voting system protection strategies.
talks.summary:
Alex Stanev presents a technical and operational case study on the deployment of electronic voting machines in Bulgaria, detailing lessons learned from the May 2019 European Parliament elections.

[05:13] Stanev describes the Bulgarian electoral process, explaining how 3,000 leased Smartmatic touch-screen direct-recording electronic (DRE) voting machines equipped with paper audit printers were deployed across polling stations nationwide. He walks through the official polling station protocols and the operational requirements for certifying and initializing machines prior to election day.

[11:16] The talk documents significant logistical and operational failures encountered during the deployment. Stanev details instances of missing or unauthenticated USB flash drives, defective smart cards used by voters to activate voting sessions, and widespread confusion among poll workers regarding machine tally reconciliation [23:25]. He highlights substantial discrepancies between the printed machine paper rolls and the handwritten polling station protocol sheets, illustrating how poorly trained staff and inadequate software verification protocols undermined public confidence in the electronic voting transition.
